newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BPS fiscally irresponsible - NBNZ Business Outlook.
newsitem.headline: BPS fiscally irresponsible - NBNZ Business Outlook.

text.p: The coalition government's first Budget Policy Statement is based on over-optimistic economic projections, has no safety net of budget surpluses and is not anchored by total government spending, the National Bank of New Zealand Ltd said on Thursday.
"If this does not raise public concern then the Fiscal Responsibility Act is belly-up," chief economist Adrian Orr wrote in the bank's March Business Outlook.

The BPS, released in early March, was based on projections from the Treasury, which gave a more bullish of the country's economic prospects than the Reserve Bank's economic projections released shortly after.
Orr said the use of the Treasury's "overly optimistic" forecasts and the wild historical variation in the fiscal projections suggested the BPS was far from responsible.
He said the Fiscal Responsibility Act (1994), intended to sharpen public scrutiny of the government's fiscal plans, appeared to have failed.
"Not only has government spending rapidly crept upward, but the government's broad fiscal objectives have been greatly diluted.

"The latest government objective to disappear is running budget surpluses of at least three percent of GDP until net debt is low. Previously this was viewed as the minimum buffer necessary to guarantee continued debt repayment."
